mainTopic: How many people a בית דין needs, the reason for רבן גמליאל's rule against cancelling a גט, and whether such a cancellation works.
overview: This עמוד opens with the end of the argument between רב נחמן and רב שֵׁשֶׁת over whether two people can count as a בית דין. רב נחמן brings proofs from the wording of a פרוזבול and from a משנה that lists judges and witnesses side by side, and רב שֵׁשֶׁת pushes both aside. The גמרא then explains why that משנה mentions both groups: the פרוזבול's wording does not have to match who signs it. Next, the גמרא asks what 'מפני תיקון העולם' means in רבן גמליאל's rule against cancelling a גט elsewhere. רבי יוחנן says it prevents ממזרים, and ריש לקיש says it helps עגונות. Each reason fits one side of the two-or-three argument. A ברייתא then asks whether a forbidden cancellation still works. רבי says it does, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it does not. The גמרא explains how the חכמים can cancel a marriage that is valid by Torah law: every קידושין is made on their terms. Finally, a new ברייתא about a husband who told ten people to write a גט begins to tie their argument to the rule of עדות שבטלה מקצתה, and that explanation continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: End of the פרוזבול quote naming only two judges
steps.stepSummary: The quote of the פרוזבול ends with 'so-and-so and so-and-so, the judges in such-and-such a place.' רב נחמן uses this as his proof that two judges are called a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...so-and-so and so-and-so, the judges in such-and-such a place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the wording of a פרוזבול. The quote names only two people and still calls them 'the judges.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרוזבול is handed over to a בית דין. Since the text names just two people and calls them 'the judges,' רב נחמן reads this as proof that two people can form a בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: So-and-so; a placeholder for a person's name
A document handing one's debts over to a בית דין so they are not cancelled by שמיטה

phrases.english: so-and-so and so-and-so, the judges
who are in such-and-such a place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote that began before this section, which is רב נחמן's first proof.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that two judges are called a בית דין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The standard wording of a פרוזבול, which names only two judges

steps.title: רב שֵׁשֶׁת: the תנא was not listing every judge
steps.stepSummary: רב שֵׁשֶׁת says the double 'so-and-so' is not a count of the judges. The תנא is not a peddler who has to list every item.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שֵׁשֶׁת? Should the תנא keep counting like a peddler?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שֵׁשֶׁת pushes away רב נחמן's proof from the פרוזבול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שֵׁשֶׁת says the wording only shows that you write in the judges' names. It was never meant to tell us how many judges there are. Writing 'so-and-so' a third time would just be pointless listing, like a peddler calling out his wares.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a rhetorical rejection)

steps.confusionAlert: רב שֵׁשֶׁת does not agree that two judges are enough. He only says this text does not prove it.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet?
phrases.notes: Short for: and how would רב שֵׁשֶׁת answer this proof?

phrases.english: Is that to say that the tanna, like a peddler,
should keep on counting?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת – אַטּוּ תַּנָּא כִּי רוֹכְלָא לִיחְשֹׁיב וְלֵיזִיל
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the פרוזבול's wording
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The double 'so-and-so' tells us to name the judges. It does not set their number.

steps.title: רב נחמן's second proof: judges compared to witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes a משנה in which either judges or witnesses sign the פרוזבול. He argues that judges are like witnesses, so two judges are enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Where do I get this from? From the משנה: 'The judges sign below, or the witnesses.' Doesn't this mean judges are like witnesses? Just as witnesses are two, judges are also two.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a new source for his view, this time from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists judges and witnesses side by side as people who can sign. רב נחמן reads them as equal in number. Since two witnesses are enough, two judges should be enough too.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a speaker's own source)
As we learned in a משנה
What, is it not...? (introduces an inference from a source)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: From where do I say it?

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: הַדַּיָּינִים חוֹתְמִין לְמַטָּה, אוֹ הָעֵדִים.
phrases.english: As we learned: The judges sign below, or the witnesses.
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in שביעית about the פרוזבול.

phrases.english: What, is it not that judges are like witnesses?
Just as the witnesses are two,
so too the judges are also two?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed aside, רב נחמן offers a second one.
steps.raayaObject: Two judges count as a בית דין
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שביעית: 'הדיינים חותמין למטה או העדים'

steps.title: רב שֵׁשֶׁת: judges and witnesses each keep their own number
steps.stepSummary: רב שֵׁשֶׁת says the comparison does not work. Judges stay three as they normally are, and witnesses stay two as they normally are.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שֵׁשֶׁת? Are they comparable? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שֵׁשֶׁת rejects the second proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Listing judges and witnesses in one sentence does not make them the same size. Each group keeps its usual number: three for judges and two for witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? (rejects a comparison between two cases)
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet? Are they comparable?!
This is as it is, and that is as it is.
phrases.notes: He means judges are their usual three and witnesses are their usual two.

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן tried two proofs that two judges make a בית דין, the פרוזבול's wording and the משנה pairing judges with witnesses. רב שֵׁשֶׁת rejected both.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between judges and witnesses
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being listed together in one sentence does not mean they have the same number.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention both judges and witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה in שביעית needs to mention both judges and witnesses as signers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need it to teach 'judges,' and why do I need it to teach 'witnesses'?
steps.whatsHappening: Moving away from the argument, the גמרא asks a question about the wording of that משנה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If either group may sign, it seems one would be enough to mention. The גמרא wants to know what we gain from hearing about both.

keyTerms.meaning: To teach; to state in the משנה

phrases.english: Why do I need it to teach 'judges,'
why do I need it to teach 'witnesses'?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנֵא דַּיָּינִים, לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנֵא עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the wording of the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the משנה teaches by naming both judges and witnesses

steps.title: The פרוזבול's wording does not have to match its signers
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a פרוזבול is valid whether it is written in judges' language and signed by witnesses, or written in witnesses' language and signed by judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us this: it makes no difference if it is written in the language of judges and witnesses sign, and no difference if it is written in the language of witnesses and judges sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming both groups shows that the wording and the signers do not have to match. What counts is that the פרוזבול was properly made. Its exact phrasing is not what matters.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: A פרוזבול is valid even if its wording does not match who signed it.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that there is no difference whether it is written in the language of judges
and witnesses sign,
and no difference whether it is written in the language of witnesses
and judges sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּלָא שְׁנָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mentioning both groups teaches that the wording and the signers can be mismatched and the פרוזבול is still valid.

steps.title: What does 'for the betterment of the world' mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's reason, 'מפני תיקון העולם', and asks what problem the rule fixes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the rule was made 'for the betterment of the world.' What does that mean here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words of the משנה and asks what danger רבן גמליאל was preventing. It is setting up the next step, where two אמוראים give answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about how many people must be present when the husband cancels the גט. Now the גמרא asks why the rule exists at all. 'תיקון העולם' is a general phrase, so it needs to be made specific.

keyTerms.meaning: Betterment of the world; a rule חז״ל made to protect society

phrases.english: For the betterment of the world:
phrases.notes: These words come from the משנה, which says a husband may not cancel the גט in a court somewhere else.

phrases.english: What is 'for the betterment of the world'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about the number of judges and asks about the reason for the משנה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What danger the rule against cancelling a גט elsewhere is meant to prevent.

steps.title: Two answers: preventing ממזרים or helping עגונות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the rule is to prevent ממזרים. ריש לקיש says it is to help עגונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is to prevent ממזרים. ריש לקיש said: it is to help עגונות.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. Each names a different danger that the rule prevents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן worries that a woman will remarry using a גט that was secretly cancelled, so her children would be ממזרים. ריש לקיש worries that women will be afraid to remarry at all, in case the גט was cancelled, and will be left stuck as עגונות.

keyTerms.meaning: A fix or protection set up by the רבנן
Children born from a forbidden union, such as a married woman with another man

steps.confusionAlert: 'תקנת ממזרים' does not mean helping ממזרים. It means preventing ממזרים from being born.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because of the fix regarding mamzerim.
phrases.notes: He means preventing children from being born as ממזרים.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Because of the fix regarding deserted wives.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי תַּקָּנַת מַמְזֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 with two different reasons.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: to prevent ממזרים. ריש לקיש: to help עגונות.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason fits רב נחמן's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן agrees with רב נחמן that a cancellation in front of two people works. Two people do not spread news, so the wife may never hear and may remarry, which produces ממזרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says the reason is to prevent ממזרים because he agrees with רב נחמן that the husband can cancel the גט in front of two people. Something done in front of two does not become known. She does not hear about it, she does not know, she goes and marries, and there are ממזרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן chose the ממזרים reason. It ties his view to רב נחמן's side of the earlier argument about two judges or three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two people are enough to cancel, the cancellation can happen quietly. The wife thinks she is divorced, remarries, and her children are ממזרים. רבן גמליאל's rule stops the husband from cancelling far from her, so this cannot happen.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like... (agrees with that view)
A voice; publicity, news that spreads

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר מִפְּנֵי תַּקָּנַת מַמְזֵרִים –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan, who said 'because of the fix regarding mamzerim' —
holds like Rav Nachman,
who said it can be done in front of two;
phrases.notes: This is the earlier argument: רב נחמן said two people are enough to cancel the גט.

phrases.english: and something done before two has no publicity;
and she does not hear and does not know
and she goes and gets married,
and there are mamzerim.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר מִפְּנֵי תַּקָּנַת מַמְזֵרִים – סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי יוחנן's answer from step 8 by linking it to רב נחמן's view from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because a cancellation before two is not publicized, the danger is that she remarries unknowingly and has ממזרים.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's reason fits רב ששת's view
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש agrees with רב ששת that three people are needed. Three people do spread news, so the wife would hear and not remarry. There is no ממזרים danger, so the reason must be עגונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says the reason is to help עגונות because he agrees with רב ששת that the cancellation must be in front of three. Something done in front of three becomes known. She hears, she knows, and she does not marry. So the only concern is the fix for עגונות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש could not use the ממזרים reason. It ties his view to רב ששת's side of the earlier argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With three people the news spreads, so a woman would not remarry by mistake and the ממזרים danger falls away. What is left is the opposite problem: women may be afraid to remarry at all. The rule protects them from being left as עגונות.

keyTerms.meaning: It becomes known; the news spreads

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא's reason matches one side of the two-or-three argument. If two are enough (רב נחמן), the danger is ממזרים (רבי יוחנן). If three are needed (רב ששת), the danger is עגונות (ריש לקיש).

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר מִפְּנֵי תַּקָּנַת עֲגוּנוֹת –
phrases.english: And Reish Lakish, who said 'because of the fix regarding deserted wives' —
holds like Rav Sheshet,
who said it must be done in front of three;
and something done before three has publicity;
and she hears and knows and does not get married;
so it is only the fix for deserted wives that applies.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר מִפְּנֵי תַּקָּנַת עֲגוּנוֹת – סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the parallel explanation for ריש לקיש, set against רבי יוחנן's in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because a cancellation before three is publicized, there is no ממזרים danger. The rule exists to help עגונות.

steps.title: If the husband cancels anyway, does it work?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי says that if the husband cancelled the גט despite the rule, it is cancelled. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he cannot cancel it or add to its conditions, because otherwise the court's power would mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if he cancelled it, it is cancelled. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: he can neither cancel it nor add to its condition. If he could, what would the power of the בית דין be worth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new question. What happens if a husband ignores רבן גמליאל's rule and cancels the גט anyway?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that the rule only says what the husband should not do. If he does it, the cancellation still works. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the cancellation does not work at all, because a rule of בית דין must have real force.

keyTerms.meaning: He cancelled it, and it is cancelled

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument decides whether a rule of חז״ל only tells a person what not to do, or actually changes the result when he breaks it.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If he cancelled it, it is cancelled; these are the words of Rabbi.
phrases.notes: He means a husband who ignored רבן גמליאל's rule and cancelled the גט away from her.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He is unable either to cancel it
or to add to its condition,
for if so,
what strength does the court have?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בִּטְּלוֹ – מְבוּטָּל, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason for the rule to what happens when someone breaks it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: a cancellation made against the rule still works. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: it does not work, nor can he add conditions, so that the court's rule keeps its force.

steps.title: How can the court permit a woman who is still married by Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. If by Torah law the husband really cancelled the גט, she is still married, so how can a reason like מה כח בית דין יפה let her marry someone else?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really a case where, by Torah law, the גט is cancelled, and yet just because of 'what is the power of the court,' we allow a married woman to marry anyone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the last step. It asks how a rabbinic reason can allow a married woman to remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, a husband can cancel a גט before it reaches his wife, so the cancelled גט is worthless and she is still an אשת איש. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל ignores the cancellation to protect the court's authority. The problem is that this seems to allow a real אשת איש to remarry, which is a very serious איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the power of the court worth? (the reason given by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל)

phrases.english: And is there anything
where by Torah law the bill of divorce is void
and because of 'what is the power of the court worth'
phrases.notes: This is the reason רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gave in the ברייתא just before this.

phrases.english: we permit a married woman to marry anyone?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that the husband's cancellation does not work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic reason should not be able to allow a woman who is married by Torah law to marry someone else.

steps.title: Every marriage depends on the approval of the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: Yes, it is possible. Every man who marries does so on the terms of the חכמים, so the חכמים can cancel his קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. Anyone who marries a woman marries her on the terms set by the חכמים, and the חכמים took his קידושין away from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים can undo the marriage itself. Then she is not a married woman at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman is not allowed to marry while she is still an אשת איש. Instead, the קידושין are cancelled from the start, so there is no marriage left. The חכמים can do this because every קידושין is made on their terms.

keyTerms.meaning: On the terms of the חכמים, with their approval

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, called אפקעינהו רבנן לקידושין מיניה, explains how the חכמים can cancel a marriage that is valid by Torah law.

phrases.english: Yes, anyone who marries
marries on the terms of the Sages,
and the Sages took the betrothal away from him.

steps.terutzResolutionType: New principle: the חכמים can cancel the marriage itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought she would still be a married woman, and the חכמים were simply allowing her to remarry.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים cancel the קידושין from the start, so she is not married at all.

steps.title: What if the marriage was made through ביאה?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי: this explanation works when he married her with money, but what about a marriage made through ביאה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: That works if he married her with money. If he married her through ביאה, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the answer of step 13. It seems to work only for one way of marrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With money, the חכמים can take the money away from the man, so no קידושין ever happened. With ביאה there is no object to take away, because the act already happened. So how can the חכמים cancel that?

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
It works well where he married her with money,
but if he married her through intercourse, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי תִּינַח
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the חכמים take the קידושין away.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking away money makes sense, but there is nothing to take away when the marriage was made through ביאה.

steps.title: The חכמים treat that act as בעילת זנות
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים declared his act to be בעילת זנות, which does not create a marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים made his ביאה into בעילת זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא. The חכמים simply say the act does not count as קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not need to take an object away. They decide that the act itself is בעילת זנות and not a marriage act. So the קידושין through ביאה are cancelled too.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it, they declared it
Relations outside of marriage, which do not create קידושין

steps.whatToRemember: When a marriage goes against the rules of the חכמים, they can cancel the קידושין. If he married with money, they take the money away. If he married through ביאה, they treat it as בעילת זנות.

phrases.english: The Sages made his intercourse into licentious intercourse.

steps.terutzResolutionType: The חכמים change how the act is legally treated.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without an object to take away, we thought קידושין through ביאה could not be cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים declare the act to be בעילת זנות, so no קידושין took effect.

steps.title: Cancelling instructions given to ten people
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: a husband told ten people to write a גט. רבי says he can cancel it in front of some of them, even when the others are not there. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he can cancel it only when they are all together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: If a man told ten people, 'Write a גט for my wife,' he can cancel it in front of one of them even when the others are not there. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: He can cancel it only when they are all present together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about a husband who gives the job of writing a גט to a group of ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that cancelling in front of only part of the group is enough. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the cancellation works only when the whole group is there. The גמרא will next ask what this argument depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: Write a גט for my wife
One without the other being present
One in front of the other, meaning all together

steps.confusionAlert: In both ברייתות (step 11 and here), רבי is the one who lets the husband's cancellation work, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is stricter. Here the question is only whether all ten must be present when he cancels.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: If he said to ten people:
'Write a bill of divorce for my wife,'

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לְבַטֵּל זֶה שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי זֶה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי.
phrases.english: he can cancel it in front of this one, not in front of that one; these are the words of Rabbi.
phrases.notes: He means he can cancel it in front of some of the ten even when the rest are not there.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְבַטֵּל אֶלָּא זֶה בִּפְנֵי זֶה.
phrases.english: He can cancel it only with this one in front of that one.
phrases.notes: In other words, all ten have to be there together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, this time about cancelling instructions given to a group of ten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: he can cancel it in front of some of them. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: he can cancel it only in front of all of them together.

steps.title: What is the basis of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל are arguing about.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short question that sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains the root of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know the general rule behind the two opinions, not just the ruling in this case.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the argument in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that divides רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: They argue about testimony that is partly cancelled
steps.stepSummary: They argue about whether testimony that is partly cancelled is completely cancelled. The גמרא begins to explain רבי's view, and the sentence continues past this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about testimony that was partly cancelled: is all of it cancelled? רבי holds: testimony that was partly cancelled...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument depends on the rule of עדות שבטלה מקצתה. It starts to explain רבי's view, and the explanation continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten people are treated like one group of witnesses. So the question is whether cancelling the job for some of them cancels it for the whole group. Each opinion matches a different side of this rule.

phrases.english: About testimony that was partly cancelled
whether all of it is cancelled, they disagree;
Rabbi holds: testimony that was partly cancelled

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעֵדוּת שֶׁבָּטְלָה מִקְצָתָהּ בָּטְלָה כּוּלָּהּ קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument depends on whether testimony that was partly cancelled is completely cancelled.
